- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or contains recent sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 73), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 2–5% of spike magnitude.  
- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a +1–2% bias to first 5 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast by averaging adjacent values.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift downward; apply +0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
